unit.title: Reported speech
unit.subtitle: decir / preguntar que and the tense shifts of “he said that…”

grammar.title: Passing on what someone said
grammar.intro: When you report someone's words in the past — “She said that she was tired” — Spanish shifts the tense back. Introduce statements with decir que, questions with preguntar si, and requests with pedir que + subjunctive. Learn the three main shifts and you can retell any conversation.

sections.heading: The three tense shifts
sections.body: When the reporting verb is in the past (dijo), the reported verb steps back one tense:

ex.en: “I'm tired” → He said he was tired.
“I'll go tomorrow” → He said he would go tomorrow.

sections.heading: Reporting questions: preguntar si
sections.body: Yes/no questions become preguntó si (asked whether). Question words (qué, dónde…) stay, but the tense still shifts:

ex.en: “Are you coming?” → He asked me whether I was coming.
“Where do you live?” → She asked where I lived.

sections.heading: Reporting requests: pedir que + subjunctive
sections.body: A command or request becomes pedir que + the imperfect subjunctive:

ex.en: “Help me” → He asked me to help him.

takeaways: Statements: decir que; questions: preguntar si; requests: pedir que + subjunctive.
present → imperfect, preterite → pluperfect, future → conditional.
«Voy» → Dijo que iba. «Iré» → Dijo que iría.
Reported yes/no questions use si: Me preguntó si venía.

mistakes.why: After a past reporting verb, the present voy shifts to the imperfect iba.
A reported preterite shifts to the pluperfect: había comido.
After pedir que, use the subjunctive (ayudara), not the present indicative.

exercises.prompt: «Voy al cine» → Dijo que ___ al cine.
exercises.prompt_en: “I'm going to the cinema” → He said he was going to the cinema.
exercises.no: The present “voy” shifts to the imperfect: “Dijo que iba”.

exercises.prompt_en: “I'll go tomorrow” → He said he would go tomorrow.
exercises.no: The future “iré” shifts to the conditional: “Dijo que iría”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “He said that he was tired.”
exercises.no: “Dijo que estaba cansado” — the present shifts to the imperfect.

exercises.prompt_en: “I ate” → He said he had eaten.
exercises.hint: Preterite shifts to the pluperfect: haber + comido.
exercises.no: The preterite shifts to the pluperfect: “Dijo que había comido”.

exercises.prompt: Match each direct quote to its reported form.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! Los cambios de tiempo están claros.

exercises.no: It was: “Dijo que estaba cansado.” (He said he was tired.)

exercises.scenario: You're relaying a message from Pablo 💬
exercises.no: His future “llegaré” shifts to the conditional after a past verb: “Me dijo que llegaría tarde”.

exercises.say: Me preguntó si venía a la fiesta
exercises.en: He asked me whether I was coming to the party
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “preguntó si venía”.
